newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ holds $1 billion of spending in "contingency".
newsitem.headline: NZ holds $1 billion of spending in "contingency".

text.p: The New Zealand government has committed NZ$3.3 billion of the coalition government's planned $5 billion in spending over the next three years, but $1 billion of the committed funds have been held in contingency, Finance Minister Bill Birch said on Friday.

"Plainly in the first of these three years we are committing $3.3 billion out of $5 billion, with $1.7 billion left for policy initiatives in the following two years," Birch said in a speech to a business breakfast.
One billion was being held in contingency, he added.
"Some of that billion dollars is there to cover a negotiated settlement of future unified pay scale for teachers. Some of it covers area of policy still being crystallized," Birch said.
The centre right coalition government tabled its first Budget on Thursday, outlining a planned surplus of $1.5 billion and $900 million of extra spending in the 1997/98 year.
Birch said the current period could not be taken as typical for this or any other government.
"There is an element of catch-up involved at present after the rigours involved in a decade of successful reform," he said.
